subject: APAC edge pilot readiness — proposed mitigation & capacity plan
messages:
From: Will Turner <will@pilotscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06T16:12:00Z
Subject: PilotScale APAC pilot — quick capacity question

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to accelerate a 6-week APAC pilot focused on low-latency chat and embeddings for our Asia-Pacific customers. Two quick questions to scope the pilot: 1) what minimum dedicated node footprint would you recommend for ~5M tokens/day during peak with realtime latency SLO of <=120ms p50, and 2) how fast can Redwood commit nodes in Singapore if we need a hard start in 6 weeks?

We expect ~10 concurrent active sessions at peak, models will be a 13B mixed-quant model, and we plan a steady ramp (pilot week 1: 20% traffic, week 6: 100%). We can share traffic profiles and a short dataset for profiling — Sara (cc) will follow up.

Thanks,
Will
--
Will Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships, PilotScale
will@pilotscale.com
+61 412 555 019

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Will Turner <will@pilotscale.com>
Cc: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@pilotscale.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-06T18:40:00Z
Subject: Re: PilotScale APAC pilot — quick capacity question

Hi Will / Sara,

Appreciate the detail — excited to get PilotScale into APAC. High-level answers up front: we can usually provision a small APAC dedicated slab in 4-8 weeks depending on spare capacity; for a conservative SLO buffer I recommend starting the pilot on a 3-node dedicated pool (each node = 8xA100-like slices) with autoscale burst to 5 nodes for peak. That aligns with ~5M tokens/day and the 120ms p50 target for the 13B quantized variant.

I've attached a quick estimate (pilot_capacity_estimate.xlsx) and an APAC node topology diagram (apac-node-topology.pdf). Next steps I propose:
- You share a day-of-week token/time distribution and a few representative prompts
- We run a short profiling pass against a sample to validate the 3-node baseline
- If profiling hits higher KV cache churn, we switch to a 4-node baseline and keep burst enabled

Lauren, looping you for contracting cadence (SOW timing + any procurement gating). Ben — can you confirm whether we have capacity hold levers for Singapore region in the 6-week window?

Irene — any hard constraints on provisioning (network, compliance, on-prem partner) we should call out?

Best,
Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 9123

Attachments: pilot_capacity_estimate.xlsx (excel stub), apac-node-topology.pdf (diagram stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PilotScale APAC pilot — quick capacity question

Hannah / team,

Checked pool availability: Singapore region shows constrained spare capacity for week-of-2027-07-18 start (our expected 6-week runway). Current options:
1) Soft reserve: we can tag 3-node slab as earmarked for PilotScale for 6 weeks (no hard commit) — provisioning ~5 business days once onboarding approved.
2) Reserve/Commit: 3-node slab reserved with a 3-month minimum (requires PO / SOW) — provisioning within 2-3 business days after contract acceptance.
3) Hybrid: start with 2-node soft reserve + autoscale burst to cloud-backed nodes (higher egress and slightly higher tail latency risk) while contract completes.

Cost delta: hybrid option ~+18% token cost during peak vs dedicated-reserve; reserve/commit is most cost-effective and gives the fastest provisioning window if procurement can sign SOW quickly.

I attached a compact estimate matrix in the pilot_capacity_estimate.xlsx tab "scenarios" — numbers assume model perf from our 13B quant baseline. If you want I can re-run with your sample prompts to give a tighter lower and upper bound.

Ben
--
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Note: capacity hold levers require signoff from Partnerships for >4 week hard commits (Lauren).

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: PilotScale APAC pilot — quick capacity question

Hannah / Ben,

Operational notes from infra/compliance:
- Singapore nodes require our standard network peering and NTP bastion; provisioning team estimates 5-7 business days from allocation.
- Data residency: PilotScale asked for regional residency; if they sign the standard data residency addendum we can restrict logs and artifacts to the APAC cluster.
- Backup plan: if we cannot secure spare SG capacity, we should stand up a hybrid fallback (2 dedicated + burst) and implement a lease-based buffer policy (auto-scale down to 1 node outside business hours).

I suggest we include an SLO escalation clause in the SOW around latency regressions during autoscale bursts and specify an agreed profiling window (48 hours) before full traffic ramp.

I can draft the ops-runbook snippet and the profiling checklist — attaching a draft mutual_action_plan_draft.docx.

Irene
--
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Will Turner <will@pilotscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@pilotscale.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PilotScale APAC pilot — quick capacity question

Hannah — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We reviewed the scenarios with our infra team and want to proceed with the hybrid start: 2-node soft reserve + burst for the first 2 weeks, then move to a 3-node reserved slab contingent on SOW signing. Can you: 1) send a short SOW draft with the reserve option and the SLO escalation clause, and 2) schedule the profiling window — week of 2027-06-21 works for us.

We'll upload the sample prompts to the Drive link you shared and Sara will follow up with the PO cadence.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to a smooth APAC ramp.

Best,
Will
